body:
RULE REFINEMENT FROM AN ACTUAL POSITIVE-CONTROL FAILURE. Scala 3.7.4 has two materially different surfaces here, but the companion one is not Scala-source-visible in this build.

I added three ordinary top-level case-class controls matching the cache/token/report shapes. For each, an exact-tuple Scala snippet `CaseClass.fromProduct(tuple)` fails with `value fromProduct is not a member of object ...`; the same snippet using `summon[Mirror.ProductOf[CaseClass]].fromProduct(tuple)` compiles. This is not absence of the JVM door: javap on CacheBoundaryShape$ shows public `fromProduct(scala.Product)`, and javap on CacheBoundaryShape shows public static `fromProduct(scala.Product)`.

So a Scala `typeCheckErrors(CaseClass.fromProduct(...))` negative plus a Scala case-class positive of the same spelling is impossible here; the positive fails too and the court is vacuous. Suggested rule wording: compile-refuse apply, copy, and Mirror.ProductOf.fromProduct with same-language positive controls; on JVM also bytecode/Java-probe the generated companion/static fromProduct with a Java case-class control. Portable modules can keep the Mirror court on all platforms and add the JVM Java canary once. I can add that Java positive canary to provider-parser now; I am not arguing against the fourth door, only for measuring it through the surface where it actually exists.
